title: Pulling back sections over an etale object along a base change is pulling back along the morphism (unit compatibility with etale localization)
statement:
Let $g:Y\to X$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] and $p:W\to X$ an etale morphism [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Let $W'$ be a scheme with morphisms $g':W'\to W$ and $p':W'\to Y$ such that $p\circ g'=g\circ p'$ and the induced morphism $\iota=(g',p'):W'\to W\times_XY$ to the fibre product of $p$ and $g$ [def-pc-fibre-product] is an isomorphism (a cartesian square); then $p'$ is etale (a base change of $p$, [lem-weil-pbc-etale-base-change-finite-limits] (1)), so $(W,p)$ is an object of $X_{\Et}$, $(W',p')$ and $(W\times_XY,\mathrm{pr}_2)$ are objects of $Y_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], and $\iota$ is an isomorphism in $Y_{\Et}$. Use the abelian sheaves [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves], the direct images $(u_*H)(T)=H(T\times_{\mathrm{target}}\mathrm{source})$ [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] and the inverse images $u^{-1}$ with units $\eta_u:\mathrm{id}\to u_*u^{-1}$ [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image]; for a sheaf $H$ on $W'_{\Et}$ read $\Gamma(W,g'_*H)=H(W\times_WW')$ as $H(W')$ through the isomorphism $(g',\mathrm{id}_{W'}):W'\to W\times_WW'$ of $W'$-schemes. For an abelian sheaf $F$ on $X_{\Et}$ let $\rho_F:p^{-1}F\xrightarrow{\sim}F|_W$ and $\rho_{g^{-1}F}:p'^{-1}g^{-1}F\xrightarrow{\sim}(g^{-1}F)|_{W'}$ be the isomorphisms of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-inverse-image-restriction] (1), so that $\rho_F(W):\Gamma(W,p^{-1}F)\xrightarrow{\sim}F(W)$ and $\rho_{g^{-1}F}(W'):\Gamma(W',p'^{-1}g^{-1}F)\xrightarrow{\sim}(g^{-1}F)(W')$, and let $\kappa_F=c_{g,p',F}^{-1}\circ c_{p,g',F}:g'^{-1}p^{-1}F\xrightarrow{\sim}(p\circ g')^{-1}F=(g\circ p')^{-1}F\xrightarrow{\sim}p'^{-1}g^{-1}F$, with $c$ the composition isomorphisms of [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition]. Then for every $a\in\Gamma(W,p^{-1}F)$
$$\rho_{g^{-1}F}(W')\Bigl(\kappa_F(W')\bigl(\eta_{g',p^{-1}F}(W)(a)\bigr)\Bigr)=(g^{-1}F)(\iota)\Bigl(\eta_{g,F}(W)\bigl(\rho_F(W)(a)\bigr)\Bigr)\quad\text{in }(g^{-1}F)(W'),$$
where $\eta_{g,F}(W):F(W)\to(g_*g^{-1}F)(W)=(g^{-1}F)(W\times_XY)$ and $(g^{-1}F)(\iota)$ is the restriction along $\iota:W'\to W\times_XY$. In words: under the identifications of the inverse image along an etale morphism with the restriction, pulling back sections along the base change $g':W'\to W$ is pulling back sections along $g$. (For an open immersion $p$ this is [lem-weil-pbc-open-restriction-pullback-unit].)

source.place: not stated in the source as such (agent-identified gap, needed by lem-weil-pbc-limit-pullback-sections-colimit, step 5); it is the unit-side counterpart of Sites, Lemma 03CF (lemma-localize-morphism: $f'_*j_U^{-1}=j_V^{-1}f_*$ for the localized morphism of sites $f':\mathcal C/U\to\mathcal D/V$, $U=u(V)$), with Lemma 03EF (lemma-localize-morphism-strong) for sites with fibre products such as the small etale sites. Intended proof (agent), as for the open-immersion case lem-weil-pbc-open-restriction-pullback-unit but without the monomorphism shortcut: both sides are $W$-sections of morphisms of sheaves $p^{-1}F\to g'_*(p'^{-1}g^{-1}F)$ on $W_{\Et}$; by $p^{-1}\dashv p_*$ they agree once their composites with $\eta_{p,F}$ agree, which is checked on each object $T$ of $X_{\Et}$ using the unit equation of $c$ (lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition (2), for both factorizations of $p\circ g'=g\circ p'$), the description of the units of $p$ and $p'$ as restrictions (lem-weil-pbc-etale-inverse-image-restriction (2)) and the naturality of $\eta_g$.

proof.text: **Step 1 (notation; the comparison morphism $\gamma$).** Put $h=p\circ g'=g\circ p':W'\to X$. The schemes and maps used below are fibre products [def-pc-fibre-product] read off from $(u_*H)(T)=H(T\times_{\mathrm{target}}\mathrm{source})$ [def-weil-pbc-direct-image], with $u_*$ acting on a morphism $f$ of the site by $H(f\times\mathrm{id})$ (the base-change functor $b_u$ of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-base-change-finite-limits] (1)): $P_0=W\times_XW$ (fibre product of $p$ with $p$; object $b_p(W)$ of $W_{\Et}$ via the second projection $\mathrm{pr}_2$, and $\mathrm{pr}_1:P_0\to W$ the counit morphism of $X_{\Et}$ of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-localization-functor-adjoint] (3)); $P_1=W\times_XY$ (object of $Y_{\Et}$ via $\mathrm{pr}_2$); $Q=W\times_XW'$ (fibre product of $p$ and $h$, object of $W'_{\Et}$ via $\mathrm{pr}_2$). Define morphisms of schemes by their components [def-pc-fibre-product]: the diagonal $\delta=(\mathrm{id}_W,\mathrm{id}_W):W\to P_0$; $\theta=(g',\mathrm{id}_{W'}):W'\to W\times_WW'$ (the isomorphism of $W'$-schemes through which the statement reads $\Gamma(W,g'_*H)$ as $H(W')$); $\tau=(\delta\circ g',\mathrm{id}_{W'}):W'\to P_0\times_WW'$ (fibre product of $\mathrm{pr}_2$ and $g'$; defined since $\mathrm{pr}_2\delta g'=g'$); $\sigma=(\iota,\mathrm{id}_{W'}):W'\to P_1\times_YW'$ (fibre product of $\mathrm{pr}_2$ and $p'$; defined since $\mathrm{pr}_2\circ\iota=p'$); $\gamma=(g',\mathrm{id}_{W'}):W'\to Q$ (defined since $p\circ g'=h$). Each is a morphism over the relevant base, hence a morphism of the small etale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-site]: $\delta:(W,\mathrm{id})\to(P_0,\mathrm{pr}_2)$ in $W_{\Et}$ (and, composing the structure maps with $p$, in $X_{\Et}$ via the functor $\iota_p$ of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-localization-functor-adjoint] (1)); $\tau$, $\sigma$, $\gamma$ are morphisms of $W'_{\Et}$ from $(W',\mathrm{id})$; $\sigma$ is also a morphism of $Y_{\Et}$ via $\iota_{p'}$. Let $\phi:P_0\times_WW'\to Q$ and $\phi':P_1\times_YW'\to Q$ be the canonical isomorphisms of [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition] (1) for $(u,v)=(p,g')$ and $(g,p')$ at the object $W$ of $X_{\Et}$, given in components by $\phi((t,w),w')=(t,w')$ and $\phi'((t,y),w')=(t,w')$, i.e. $\phi=(\mathrm{pr}_1\circ\mathrm{pr}_1,\mathrm{pr}_2)$ and $\phi'=(\mathrm{pr}_1\circ\mathrm{pr}_1,\mathrm{pr}_2)$. Comparing components: $\phi\circ\tau=(\mathrm{pr}_1\delta g',\mathrm{id})=(g',\mathrm{id})=\gamma$ and $\phi'\circ\sigma=(\mathrm{pr}_1\iota,\mathrm{id})=(g',\mathrm{id})=\gamma$ (since $\mathrm{pr}_1\circ\iota=g'$); also $\tau=(\delta\times_WW')\circ\theta$, $\mathrm{pr}_1\circ\delta=\mathrm{id}_W$ and $\mathrm{pr}_1\circ\sigma=\iota$, where $\mathrm{pr}_1:P_1\times_YW'\to P_1$. By [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition] (1), $d_{p,g',H}(W)=H(\phi)$ and $d_{g,p',H}(W)=H(\phi')$ for a sheaf $H$ on $W'_{\Et}$.

proof.text: **Step 2 (the unit of $p$ at $W$, restricted along the diagonal).** By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-inverse-image-restriction] (2) for $j=p$, $G=F$ and the object $(W,p)$ of $X_{\Et}$: $\rho_F(P_0)\circ\eta_{p,F}(W)=F(\mathrm{pr}_1):F(W)\to F(P_0)$. The isomorphism $\rho_F:p^{-1}F\to F|_W$ of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-inverse-image-restriction] (1) is a morphism of sheaves on $W_{\Et}$, so it commutes with the restriction along $\delta$: $\rho_F(W)\circ(p^{-1}F)(\delta)=F|_W(\delta)\circ\rho_F(P_0)=F(\delta)\circ\rho_F(P_0)$. Hence $\rho_F(W)\circ(p^{-1}F)(\delta)\circ\eta_{p,F}(W)=F(\delta)\circ F(\mathrm{pr}_1)=F(\mathrm{pr}_1\circ\delta)=F(\mathrm{id}_W)=\mathrm{id}$, and since $\rho_F(W)$ is bijective: $(p^{-1}F)(\delta)\circ\eta_{p,F}(W)=\rho_F(W)^{-1}$ (E1). In the same way, by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-inverse-image-restriction] (2) for $j=p'$, $G=g^{-1}F$ and the object $(P_1,\mathrm{pr}_2)$ of $Y_{\Et}$: $\rho_{g^{-1}F}(P_1\times_YW')\circ\eta_{p',g^{-1}F}(P_1)=(g^{-1}F)(\mathrm{pr}_1)$, and naturality of $\rho_{g^{-1}F}$ along $\sigma$ gives $\rho_{g^{-1}F}(W')\circ(p'^{-1}g^{-1}F)(\sigma)\circ\eta_{p',g^{-1}F}(P_1)=(g^{-1}F)(\sigma)\circ(g^{-1}F)(\mathrm{pr}_1)=(g^{-1}F)(\mathrm{pr}_1\circ\sigma)=(g^{-1}F)(\iota)$, i.e. $(p'^{-1}g^{-1}F)(\sigma)\circ\eta_{p',g^{-1}F}(P_1)=\rho_{g^{-1}F}(W')^{-1}\circ(g^{-1}F)(\iota)$ as maps $(g^{-1}F)(P_1)\to\Gamma(W',p'^{-1}g^{-1}F)$ (E2).

proof.text: **Step 3 (the unit of $h$ through $h=p\circ g'$).** Apply [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition] (2) with $u=p$, $v=g'$, $G=F$: $p_*g'_*(c_{p,g',F})\circ p_*(\eta_{g',p^{-1}F})\circ\eta_{p,F}=d_{p,g',h^{-1}F}\circ\eta_{h,F}$. Evaluate at the object $(W,p)$ of $X_{\Et}$ (a direct image acts on a morphism of sheaves componentwise, $(u_*\alpha)(T)=\alpha(T\times\ldots)$ [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]; step 1 for $d$): $c_{p,g',F}(P_0\times_WW')\circ\eta_{g',p^{-1}F}(P_0)\circ\eta_{p,F}(W)=(h^{-1}F)(\phi)\circ\eta_{h,F}(W)$ as maps $F(W)\to(h^{-1}F)(P_0\times_WW')$. Compose on the left with the restriction $(h^{-1}F)(\delta\times_WW')$ and then with $(h^{-1}F)(\theta)$, i.e. with $(h^{-1}F)(\tau)$ (step 1). On the right side this gives $(h^{-1}F)(\phi\circ\tau)\circ\eta_{h,F}(W)=(h^{-1}F)(\gamma)\circ\eta_{h,F}(W)$. On the left side, with $K=g'^{-1}p^{-1}F$: $c_{p,g',F}$ is a morphism of sheaves on $W'_{\Et}$, so it commutes with restriction along $\tau$; and the unit $\eta_{g'}:\mathrm{id}\to g'_*g'^{-1}$ [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image] is natural in the object, so along $\delta:(W,\mathrm{id})\to(P_0,\mathrm{pr}_2)$ of $W_{\Et}$, on which $g'_*K$ acts by $K(\delta\times_WW')$: $K(\delta\times_WW')\circ\eta_{g',p^{-1}F}(P_0)=\eta_{g',p^{-1}F}(W)\circ(p^{-1}F)(\delta)$. With (E1) the left side becomes $c_{p,g',F}(W')\circ K(\theta)\circ\eta_{g',p^{-1}F}(W)\circ\rho_F(W)^{-1}$, where $K(\theta)\circ\eta_{g',p^{-1}F}(W)$ is $\eta_{g',p^{-1}F}(W)$ read in $K(W')$ as in the statement; write $\bar\eta_{g'}(W)$ for it. Hence $c_{p,g',F}(W')\circ\bar\eta_{g'}(W)\circ\rho_F(W)^{-1}=(h^{-1}F)(\gamma)\circ\eta_{h,F}(W)$ as maps $F(W)\to(h^{-1}F)(W')$ (E3).

proof.text: **Step 4 (the unit of $h$ through $h=g\circ p'$).** Apply [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition] (2) with $u=g$, $v=p'$, $G=F$: $g_*p'_*(c_{g,p',F})\circ g_*(\eta_{p',g^{-1}F})\circ\eta_{g,F}=d_{g,p',h^{-1}F}\circ\eta_{h,F}$. At the object $(W,p)$ of $X_{\Et}$, as in step 3: $c_{g,p',F}(P_1\times_YW')\circ\eta_{p',g^{-1}F}(P_1)\circ\eta_{g,F}(W)=(h^{-1}F)(\phi')\circ\eta_{h,F}(W)$, with $\eta_{g,F}(W):F(W)\to(g^{-1}F)(P_1)$. Compose on the left with the restriction $(h^{-1}F)(\sigma)$. The right side becomes $(h^{-1}F)(\phi'\circ\sigma)\circ\eta_{h,F}(W)=(h^{-1}F)(\gamma)\circ\eta_{h,F}(W)$ (step 1). On the left, $c_{g,p',F}$ commutes with restriction along $\sigma$ (a morphism of sheaves on $W'_{\Et}$), and (E2) gives $c_{g,p',F}(W')\circ(p'^{-1}g^{-1}F)(\sigma)\circ\eta_{p',g^{-1}F}(P_1)\circ\eta_{g,F}(W)=c_{g,p',F}(W')\circ\rho_{g^{-1}F}(W')^{-1}\circ(g^{-1}F)(\iota)\circ\eta_{g,F}(W)$. Hence $c_{g,p',F}(W')\circ\rho_{g^{-1}F}(W')^{-1}\circ(g^{-1}F)(\iota)\circ\eta_{g,F}(W)=(h^{-1}F)(\gamma)\circ\eta_{h,F}(W)$ as maps $F(W)\to(h^{-1}F)(W')$ (E4).

proof.text: **Step 5 (conclusion).** By (E3) and (E4), $c_{p,g',F}(W')\circ\bar\eta_{g'}(W)\circ\rho_F(W)^{-1}=c_{g,p',F}(W')\circ\rho_{g^{-1}F}(W')^{-1}\circ(g^{-1}F)(\iota)\circ\eta_{g,F}(W)$. Apply $c_{g,p',F}(W')^{-1}$ (the component of the inverse of the isomorphism $c_{g,p'}$ of [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition] (2)); by the definition $\kappa_F=c_{g,p',F}^{-1}\circ c_{p,g',F}$ this reads $\kappa_F(W')\circ\bar\eta_{g'}(W)\circ\rho_F(W)^{-1}=\rho_{g^{-1}F}(W')^{-1}\circ(g^{-1}F)(\iota)\circ\eta_{g,F}(W)$. Composing with $\rho_{g^{-1}F}(W')$ on the left and $\rho_F(W)$ on the right gives $\rho_{g^{-1}F}(W')\circ\kappa_F(W')\circ\bar\eta_{g'}(W)=(g^{-1}F)(\iota)\circ\eta_{g,F}(W)\circ\rho_F(W)$, which evaluated at $a\in\Gamma(W,p^{-1}F)$ is the assertion.

lean.statement: theorem etale_restriction_pullback_unit {X Y W W' : Scheme.{u}} (g : Y ⟶ X) (p : W ⟶ X) (g' : W' ⟶ W) (p' : W' ⟶ Y) (hcomm : g' ≫ p = p' ≫ g) (ι : W' ⟶ pullback p g) (hι₁ : ι ≫ pullback.fst p g = g') (hι₂ : ι ≫ pullback.snd p g = p') [IsIso ι] [hp : Etale p] : ∃ hp' : Etale p', let A := AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1} let w : W.Etale := Scheme.Etale.mk (𝟙 W) let w' : W'.Etale := Scheme.Etale.mk (𝟙 W') let wx : X.Etale := Scheme.Etale.mk p let wy' : Y.Etale := @Scheme.Etale.mk _ _ p' hp' let eW : (MorphismProperty.Over.map ⊤ hp).obj w ≅ wx := MorphismProperty.Over.isoMk (Iso.refl W) (by simp [wx, w]) let eW' : (MorphismProperty.Over.map ⊤ hp').obj w' ≅ wy' := MorphismProperty.Over.isoMk (Iso.refl W') (by simp [wy', w']) let theta : w' ⟶ (MorphismProperty.Over.pullback @Etale ⊤ g').obj w := MorphismProperty.Over.homMk (pullback.lift g' (𝟙 W') (by exact (Category.comp_id g').trans (Category.id_comp g').symm)) (by simp [w']) let iotaSite : wy' ⟶ (MorphismProperty.Over.pullback @Etale ⊤ g).obj wx := MorphismProperty.Over.homMk ι hι₂ ∀ F : Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology A, let pF := (Etale.upperStar A p).obj F let gF := (Etale.upperStar A g).obj F let K := (Etale.upperStar A g').obj pF let rhoF := (Etale.upperStarIsoLocalizationRestriction A p hp).hom.app F let rhoG := (Etale.upperStarIsoLocalizationRestriction A p' hp').hom.app gF let kappa := (Etale.upperStarComp A g' p).inv.app F ≫ (Etale.upperStarComp A p' g (g' ≫ p) hcomm).hom.app F ((Etale.upperStarLowerStarAdjunction A g').unit.app pF).hom.app (op w) ≫ K.obj.map theta.op ≫ kappa.hom.app (op w') ≫ rhoG.hom.app (op w') ≫ gF.obj.map eW'.inv.op = rhoF.hom.app (op w) ≫ F.obj.map eW.inv.op ≫ ((Etale.upperStarLowerStarAdjunction A g).unit.app F).hom.app (op wx) ≫ gF.obj.map iotaSite.op
